headline: Answer drafts need a revision lane before learner trust.
copy: Use this workbench to compare a draft problem, the source card, the repair decision, and the revised packet.

steps.title: Read
steps.copy: Read the draft and the source card together.

steps.title: Cut
steps.copy: Remove certainty, promise, or category confusion.

steps.title: Repair
steps.copy: Rewrite in one direct answer plus one boundary.

steps.title: Record
steps.copy: Save the reason for the revision.

candidates.title: Steady action draft
candidates.reason: The answer is useful but too confident about emotional outcome.

record.title: Steady action
record.summary: Supports a practical answer about acting steadily while not turning outcomes into identity.
record.boundary: Reflection support only; not therapy, medical advice, ritual instruction, or spiritual command.

candidates.packet:
Problem: promises calm too strongly.
Revision: say the source supports steady action, not guaranteed peace.
Approved draft: Begin with one honest next action. The source points toward steadiness in action, while the result remains uncertain.
Boundary: reflection support only.

candidates.title: Oppenheimer source draft
candidates.reason: The answer corrects category confusion and keeps the tone respectful.

record.title: Oppenheimer category correction
record.summary: Supports correcting the common claim: the famous line is associated with the Gita, not the four Vedas.
record.boundary: Do not call it a direct quote from the four Vedas.

candidates.packet:
Problem: popular wording can imply direct Vedic quotation.
Revision: say Bhagavad Gita and source family explicitly.
Approved draft: The famous line is associated with Bhagavad Gita 11.32, a section of the Mahabharata usually classified as Smriti.
Boundary: do not call it a direct four-Veda quote.

candidates.title: Gayatri mantra draft
candidates.reason: Needs mantra reviewer and recitation boundary before learner-facing depth.

record.title: Gayatri mantra care
record.summary: Useful for source context, but learner-facing draft must avoid ritual instruction, pronunciation authority, or initiation claims.
record.boundary: No ritual instruction, initiation advice, or recitation authority.

candidates.packet:
Problem: draft drifts toward instruction.
Revision: route to source context only.
Approved draft: VedaPath can identify the source family and explain why the passage needs careful review before guidance.
Boundary: no ritual, initiation, or pronunciation authority.
